label: Back-on-Track

label: OpenStreetMap Relations
description: Route geometries (polylines) cached from Overpass API

label: NightJet / EuroNight
description: Official ÖBB NightJet API — accurate polylines and timetables

label: European Sleeper
description: European Sleeper timetable from the Mobility Database GTFS feed mdb-3107 — stop coordinates, real track geometry (shapes.txt) and service calendars all come from the feed, so there is nothing to scrape and no OSM geometry lookup. Routes are taken per data/sources/europeansleeper-sleepers.json, matched on route_short_name. The feed is date-expanded (one trip per operating date, calendar_dates.txt only) and each date can carry its own diversion, so the map routing is the MODAL stop sequence across future trips — see scripts/adapters/europeansleeper.mjs.

label: Czech Railways (ČD)
description: Official cd.cz EC train timetables

label: China Railway

label: Trenitalia ICN
description: Official Viaggiatreno API — Intercity Notte timetables

label: Caucasus Railways

label: Curated routes

label: Amtrak
description: Official Amtrak GTFS feed, filtered to long-distance routes with sleeping cars (data/sources/amtrak-sleepers.json). Each route becomes a synthetic map route; coordinates, polylines and service calendars come straight from the feed. Refreshed nightly inside the scrape.

label: VIA Rail Canada
description: Official VIA Rail GTFS feed, filtered to overnight routes with sleeping cars/berths (data/sources/viarail-sleepers.json). Each route becomes a synthetic map route; coordinates, polylines and service calendars come straight from the feed. Refreshed nightly inside the scrape.

label: ONCF (Morocco)
description: Official ONCF night trains (Marrakech–Tanger, Casablanca–Oujda), both with couchettes and sleeper cabins. DISABLED until the 'Probe ONCF source' workflow identifies a stable machine-readable surface — the published community GTFS (MobilityDatabase mdb-3049) expired 2025-12-31 and models zero overnight service, so it is unusable. The probe checks the oncf-voyages.ma booking API, the official timetable downloads, and the legacy /fr/Horaires search; implement scripts/adapters/oncf.mjs against the artifact, switch kind to json-api if a JSON feed exists, then enable. Until then Morocco is covered by curated routes.

label: CFR Călători
description: Official Romanian national timetable ('Mersul trenurilor') published as open data on data.gov.ro — one XML per carrier per timetable year. Rebuilds every CFR row's full stop list, official times and geometry (OSM-backed route-geometry cache, straight chain through the official stops as the floor); coordinates and canonical spellings come from Back-on-Track's station table because the XML carries neither. International trains keep Back-on-Track's foreign stretch (the file stops at the border). Probe workflow: 'Probe CFR source'. GitHub's runners cannot reach data.gov.ro — the connection is dropped rather than refused, so every run fails on the same ~10.5s connect timeout — so params.localTimetable names a committed gzipped copy of the same file, used as the fallback and reported in ctx.errors when it is. The national timetable changes once a year (second Sunday in December): refresh that file then.

label: SNCF
description: Official SNCF Open Data GTFS (TGV / Intercités / TER), filtered to the Intercités de Nuit (data/sources/sncf-sleepers.json). The feed's routes are not addresses — route_long_name is "-" for six of these eleven trains and files two of the named ones under another corridor — so the allowlist selects them as oriented endpoint pairs and keys each by Back-on-Track's own "IC Nuit NNNN" label, which is what the trainsByNumber enrichment looks a view-map row up by. Enrichment is deliberately via-only: the feed has no shapes.txt, and one route_id there carries both directions plus the portions that split at Toulouse and Brive, so the fullest trip for a pair can be a through-portion whose endpoint times are not the train's. The first live run confirmed that from two angles — endpoint times disagreed with Back-on-Track by over an hour on four of ten runs, and service days came out per-trip ("Sun" for a daily train), because a date-expanded feed gives each trip its own service_id and only one trip is picked. Stop lists survive all of that (8–16 stations against Back-on-Track's 2–5, and every stop between two fixed endpoints is on the corridor whichever trip was chosen), so updateVia is on with viaOnlyIfRicher, and setTimes/updateEndpoints/updateServiceDays/stamp stay off. Probe workflow: 'Probe GTFS feed'.

label: Vy (Entur)
description: Norway is centralised on Entur, which publishes a GTFS file per operator codespace with no key: rb_vyg-aggregated-gtfs.zip covers F4 Oslo S–Bergen (Back-on-Track row 69, trains 605/606). Every allowlist entry is a NAMED ORIENTED pair, because Entur files each night train inside a whole line that also runs day services — the trip with the most stations, which a plain route name would select, is a day train — so the entry names the train and buildSleeperTrains requires the trip to cross midnight. Enrichment is via-only: Back-on-Track gives these routes 2 to 6 via points against the feed's full stop list. Two things that richer list forces, both invisible while the via lists were sparse. Entur appends " stasjon" to every station name where the rest of the dataset writes the bare name, so params.stripStationSuffixes takes it off before the alias table runs — without it not one of the 86 stops resolves to a coordinate-bearing station and the official stop list buys no map dots at all. And once they do resolve, 27 of the 86 land on a Back-on-Track coordinate that is somewhere else entirely: every one stamped country NO, 22 of them off by more than 400 km (Tverlandet on the Basque coast, Stjørdal in Czechia, Voss in Germany, Trondheim Airport Værnes in Stockholm), so station-coordinates.json now carries the operator's own coordinate for each. The 59 that agree agree within 1.26 km and nothing at all sits between that and 5.31 km, so the threshold is not a judgement call. Times and service days stay off for the same reason as SNCF, until a night's log shows they are the train's. shapes.txt here is 108–416 MB, past MAX_SHAPES_BYTES, so geometry is the station chain through the official stops. Probe workflow: 'Probe GTFS feed'.

label: PKP Intercity (Polish GTFS)
description: Official PKP Intercity timetable data (mkuran.pl is a mechanical daily conversion of the official NAP feed), plus Leo Express sleeper shapes discovered from the same polish_trains.zip (overnight LEO trips of 12h+). Committed as public/data/gtfs/pkpTrainShapes.json; regenerated nightly inside the scrape (npm run parse-pkp-gtfs). Enriches PKP and Leo Express rows with official stop lists and stamps them for trusted auto-approval.

label: PKP / PLK Open Data (station info)
description: Official PLK 'Otwarte Dane Kolejowe' API (pdp-api.plk-sa.pl) — the infrastructure manager's authoritative planned schedule, richest for international EN/EC station lists. SUPPLEMENT: folds PLK per-train stop lists (station names + times; coords reconciled from GTFS) into the existing pkpTrainShapes.json byTrainKey bundle, keeping the GTFS/OSM geometry. Gated on /data-version so a typical night is a single request. Runs after pkp-gtfs (which regenerates the bundle nightly). Requires the PLK_API_KEY secret (absent key is a safe no-op).

label: RegioJet (GTFS timetables)
description: Checked-in artifacts public/data/gtfs/rj*.json. Regenerate manually: npm run parse-gtfs.
endpoint: gtfs-data/regiojet/ (local GTFS drop — npm run parse-gtfs)
